conclusions: Dominant observed wait: Catalog JDBC connection acquisition; 153/160/170 of 200 servlet threads; list callers 106/108/135
Two shared CPUs saturated; high-load mean idle 0.26%, I/O wait and steal 0 in sampled windows; no Catalog cgroup CPU quota throttling
Representative SQL execution remained 0.039-2.387ms under load; this does not measure application queue or JDBC time
Identity synchronous lookups add work, but do not account for most observed wait; published lookup currently spans HTTP in a DB transaction
Direct Catalog details/published probes exceeded internal gateway 2s read budget; Catalog queueing explains how internal 504 can propagate as booking 503
limitations: Single shared account, diagnostic duration and signal-based thread sampling; not a new capacity pass
No JFR/flamegraph or pool lease-duration distribution collected; CPU hot methods and best pool size not established
Lightsail CPU burst credit metrics unavailable with current local AWS credentials; sampled steal=0 is not historical credit proof
